W.note: Syllables 5-7-5 (Win-ter dusk sun gone / a veil too high for the dark / holds moth-er-of-pearl); the veil too high for the dark accurately evokes nacreous clouds lit after sunset, though the last line is a stock term.

X.note: Syllables 4-7-5 (Na-cre-ous glow = 4), so the first line is short; names nacreous and mother-of-pearl but the sky holds its breath is cliche and the images stay abstract.

Y.note: Syllables 5-7-5 (fire may count as 2, making line 3 a 6); fire on frozen air is a strong image, but nacreous light at dusk, slow is clotted and repeats the mother-of-pearl idea.

Z.note: Syllables 5-7-5 (sun gone from the street / a veil of ice up there still / burning pearl and rose); street-level vantage, ice crystals and still burning color evoke polar stratospheric clouds without naming them.
